resumeInstructions: 1. Read this checkpoint, atomic-claims.json, knowledge-graph.json, entities/gameplay-entities.json, entities/system-event-command-registry.json, priority-queues.json, and transcript-inventory.json first.
2. Run `node scripts/knowledge-tools-test.mjs` -- if anything fails, fix the DATA (not the test) unless the test itself is proven wrong.

3. Re-run `node scripts/knowledge-transcript-inventory.mjs` to refresh transcript-inventory.json/priority-queues.json, and `node scripts/knowledge-canonical-facts.mjs --write` + `node scripts/knowledge-provenance-report.mjs --write` after adding any new claims -- all 3 are generators, never hand-edit their output files directly.

4. To continue bulk claim extraction: `node scripts/knowledge-query.mjs unverified --priority=P0` or read priority-queues.json's P0 array directly for the next unprocessed videos, in the same batch-read-then-batch-write pattern used throughout Phase 5 (read 5-6 transcripts per round-trip, then append claims+KI-entries together) -- avoid the earlier phases' one-video-at-a-time pattern, it doesn't scale to 69 remaining videos.
5. Before building new MAP/EVENT entity names, check whether any captured source (video or config) ever states a map's name alongside its numeric ID -- do not guess from general MU knowledge.

6. `node scripts/knowledge-query.mjs source <videoId>` shows a single video's full pipeline status; `node scripts/knowledge-query.mjs claims <system>` and `entity/map/item/event <name>` are the fastest ways to check existing coverage before extracting a new claim, to avoid accidental duplicates.
